parts.label: Prepare
parts.title: Define incidents by business effect
parts.body:
An AI incident can be a personal-data exposure, unauthorized tool action, materially harmful or incorrect output, compromised retrieval source, model-provider outage, or uncontrolled spend. Some events are security or privacy breaches; others are quality or safety failures. A common triage path should identify the affected service, people, data, actions, time window, severity, and owner without waiting to settle a legal label.

Before release, name who can disable a tool, revoke a connector token, switch to a human workflow, rollback a configuration, and approve customer communication. Set detection signals: unusual sends, write volume, sensitive-data matches, complaint spikes, repeated correction, or provider error rate. Protect logs and maintain a configuration and model-version record sufficient to reconstruct the event. Recording every raw prompt indefinitely creates its own privacy exposure, so choose a justified retention and access design.

Define thresholds in terms of consequence and speed. An agent sending an unauthorized message calls for immediate containment even if only one message is known. A small increase in benign summary corrections may call for investigation and a limited pause. The business owner, security lead, privacy lead, legal adviser, and CAIO should know their roles before an on-call engineer faces the decision alone.

example.title: A runbook entry
example.body: Trigger: any unapproved external email sent by the service agent. On-call owner disables its send token, freezes related jobs, preserves scoped logs, identifies recipients, and convenes security, privacy, legal, and the business owner. Customer communication follows confirmed facts and applicable obligations.

exercise.title: Set three triggers
exercise.body: For an agent with email and CRM access, define one safety, one privacy, and one availability trigger. Give each a detection source, severity, first-hour containment owner, decision authority, and fallback workflow.

sources: OWASP Top 10 for LLM and GenAI applications

parts.label: Contain
parts.title: Pause the capability that can cause harm
parts.body:
Containment must match the failure path. For duplicate messages, suspend the send permission or queue, then stop scheduled retries. For a compromised retrieval source, isolate the source and invalidate the index or cache. For suspected exfiltration, revoke credentials, block the path, preserve evidence, and assess what actually left. A model rollback alone may not stop an agent whose connector has already queued actions.

Separate immediate containment from root-cause analysis. The incident commander may act on credible signals while facts are incomplete, recording what is known and why a pause is proportionate. Preserve relevant prompts, retrieved content, tool calls, configurations, identities, and timestamps under the incident retention policy. Do not delete logs to make the system look clean. Assign an owner to reconcile completed and pending actions so customers do not receive another duplicate during recovery.

Keep a manual or lower-automation alternative for essential service. If the provider is down, customer support may use approved knowledge articles and ordinary case queues. Test that fallback under a realistic workload and define who authorizes its use. The cost of resilience is part of the investment case.

example.title: Duplicate customer emails
example.body: An update causes an agent to send two messages per case. Operations disables the sending token and drains the queue; the team lists affected recipients, checks whether any message disclosed another customer's data, and restores the previous tested configuration only after a dry run. The privacy team assesses any disclosure separately.

exercise.title: Write the first-hour card
exercise.body: For the duplicate-email scenario, list the first five actions in order, the person authorized to take each, evidence to preserve, business fallback, and decision point for notifying affected people. Do not assume a legal reporting duty before facts and jurisdiction are assessed.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: contingency and monitoring

parts.label: Assess
parts.title: Separate operational response from legal notification
parts.body:
The incident commander needs a fast factual record: what happened, data and people affected, likely harm, containment time, evidence confidence, and unresolved questions. Legal and privacy leads then apply the relevant notification tests and deadlines. In the EU, GDPR Article 33 generally requires a controller to notify a supervisory authority of a personal-data breach within 72 hours after awareness unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to rights and freedoms, with reasons for delay if later; Article 34 addresses communication to affected people for high risk. Roles and facts matter.

For organizations covered by Canada's PIPEDA, breaches of security safeguards posing a real risk of significant harm must be reported to the Commissioner and notified to affected individuals as soon as feasible, and records of all breaches must be kept. The assessment considers sensitivity and probability of misuse. Provincial laws and sector rules may add or differ in duties. A quality incident without personal-data exposure may still require customer remediation or contractual notice even when a privacy breach rule does not apply.

Do not wait for perfect certainty to involve counsel. Record the awareness time, updates, rationale, and who makes each decision. A multinational incident may produce different notices for different people and regulators. Communications should state confirmed facts, protective actions, and a route for questions; avoid speculative assurances.

example.title: The same event has two tracks
example.body: A chatbot gives an incorrect refund policy to 400 customers and exposes one customer's address in another response. The business team corrects advice and remedies losses. Privacy and legal assess the address disclosure under applicable EU and Canadian regimes, preserving the timeline and facts rather than treating the entire event as one undifferentiated severity score.

exercise.title: Open a notification clock
exercise.body: For a hypothetical Berlin and Vancouver exposure, make a timeline of discovery, containment, fact gathering, counsel review, regulator decision, customer contact, and remediation. List missing facts that determine GDPR and Canadian reporting tests. State who owns each clock.

sources: Office of the Privacy Commissioner: PIPEDA breach reporting

parts.label: Recover
parts.title: Prove the fix before reopening the workflow
parts.body:
Recovery is a new release decision. Identify the cause and the path to harm, fix the control, run regression and adversarial tests, reconcile affected records, and verify that monitoring can detect a repeat. A model rollback can restore an earlier behavior but may also restore older vulnerabilities. Test the whole system, including connectors, queues, and human handoffs. Authorize staged return with a named owner and rollback trigger.

An after-action review should separate individual error from process conditions: broad permissions, weak change review, missing telemetry, unclear on-call authority, or an untested fallback. Assign corrective actions with deadlines and an effectiveness check. Report both time to detect and contain and the number of affected people or actions. Counting incidents without severity or exposure can reward hiding reports.

Tabletop exercises make the plan credible. Include an outage, malicious document, wrong answer, and unauthorized action over the year. Invite business operations, security, legal, privacy, communications, vendor management, and the CAIO where relevant. Rehearse a stop decision and customer-facing service continuity, then update the runbook based on what the team could actually do.

example.title: A staged return
example.body: After a duplicate-send incident, the team disables automatic sends, fixes queue idempotency, tests repeated retries, and resumes in draft-only mode. A trained reviewer approves messages for one week while monitoring duplicate attempts. The service executive decides when to restore automation against predefined criteria.

exercise.title: Run a 30-minute tabletop
exercise.body: Give a team a provider update, 20 duplicate emails, and a possible cross-customer disclosure. At 10-minute intervals add a new fact. Record who paused the system, what evidence they had, how fallback worked, the notification owner, and the test required to reopen. Revise the runbook.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: MANAGE and GOVERN
Office of the Privacy Commissioner: PIPEDA breach reporting
